title: List more keyboard shortcuts in the TUI
lead: Make existing keyboard actions easier to discover while browsing the roadmap, without requiring users to open the help overlay first.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** adding or remapping keyboard actions, configurable keybindings, changing roadmap operations, or redesigning the TUI beyond the space needed for shortcut hints.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The normal view starts with `? help  / search  f filters  c show all` in View.message. The BINDINGS table already includes navigation, pane switching, editing, creation, reordering, status changes, promotion, rendering, and quitting, and supplies the full `?` help overlay. These existing actions deserve more visible hints in the browsing view.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- src/slicer/tui.py: BINDINGS, View feedback, and draw layout.
- src/slicer/tui_style.py: reuse existing bounded drawing and terminal-size behavior if layout changes require it.
- tests/test_tui.py and tests/test_cli.py: drawing, mode handling, and binding/help coverage.
- README.md: document the visible hints and how to reach full help.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: Add focused rendering checks for visible shortcut hints at the supported minimum size (80x10) and a wider terminal. Cover feedback, prompts, help/filter overlays, and resizing so hints cannot obscure interaction state. Check that advertised keys map to the existing binding actions.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add a persistent shortcut strip on the main browsing screen for common existing actions: Tab panes, e edit, a add, s start, d done, / search, f filters, c show all, g jump, j/k move, ? help, and q quit. Derive keys from BINDINGS and keep concise labels with binding metadata. Use fixed defaults; defer customization and key remapping because there is no existing TUI preference configuration. Pack complete hints into one row when they fit or two rows at 80x10. Reserve the strip below the separate status and feedback rows, adjusting both panes to the remaining space. Feedback must never replace the shortcuts. Show the strip only in normal mode; retain mode-specific instructions in search, jump, filter, and help. Preserve full help, existing actions, monochrome support, and the below-minimum resize screen. Document the strip in README.md.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: At 80x10 and wider sizes, all common shortcut hints are visible without overlap; verify queue and detail scrolling with reduced content space. Verify hints persist alongside success/error feedback with either pane focused. Cover empty results, modal instructions, resizing, and consistency with BINDINGS. Run focused TUI tests, the full unit suite with workspace-local temporary files, slicer check, and git diff --check. Perform a terminal readability check at minimum and wider sizes before marking done. Fixed defaults are intentional; no preference configuration or remapping is included.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Follow owner instructions for committing and publishing.
